Every spec of a layer registers the states the project requires of it (`required_states:`).

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Checker | `states-required` |
| Confronts | `spec` |
| Blocking by default — new project | yes |
| Blocking by default — existing project | no — informs |

## How it measures

A spec registers the states its author thought of, and every state gate confronts only those.
Measured in MIF: nine released defects were a screen state nobody wrote — an error shown as an
empty list, a not-found that spun forever, an offline screen with no way back.

The project names the states each layer owes, by the layer a spec's header declares:

```yaml
required_states:
  screen: [loading, error, empty, offline]
```

Each spec of that layer registers a state by each name — a line carrying the state's code
(`SCRNX-S03`) and the name, its heading or its row —, or says why not, on a line of its own:
`@no-state: offline — the screen reads only local data`. The names are the project's: Anchors
proposes none.

## Declaring it

```yaml
gates:
  - name: states-required
    on: [spec]
    check: states-required
```

Source: [checker](https://github.com/co2-lab/anchors/blob/main/internal/gate/states_required.go) · [its spec](https://github.com/co2-lab/anchors/blob/main/internal/gate/states_required.spec.md)
